profile.reading:
The address associated with this record, 311 West Monroe Street in Chicago's Loop, is the Chicago headquarters office of West Monroe, a business and technology consulting firm. West Monroe's own website lists this address, on the 14th floor of the building, as its Chicago office, one of a network of offices the firm maintains across the United States and abroad to serve clients in financial services, healthcare, energy and utilities, and other industries.

West Monroe is not a data center operator. It is a professional services firm whose Chicago location is a leased floor of office space used for client work, consulting staff, and corporate functions, not a purpose built facility for housing servers or IT infrastructure. Firms of this kind typically rely on cloud providers and third party hosting for their own technology needs rather than operating dedicated data centers, and nothing in West Monroe's public materials or the building's own listings describes any data center function at this location.

Because this location is an office rather than a data center, there is no square footage, power capacity, or cooling specification to report for it in that sense, and none should be expected.

reading.body:
West Monroe's Chicago address is an office, not a data center, and contributes zero megawatts to Illinois data center capacity.

The record carries a power figure of 0 MW and no square footage, cooling specification, or other facility metric. The address, 311 West Monroe Street in the Loop, is listed on the firm's own website as its Chicago office, a leased floor used for consulting staff and client work. West Monroe is a management and technology consulting firm, not a data center operator, and nothing in its public materials or the building's listings describes a data center function there.

The pattern matters because it shows how facility counts can overstate infrastructure. Illinois has 44 mapped facilities, but only 6 publish power specifications, totaling 236 MW. A record like this one adds to the count while adding nothing to the capacity that constrains AI scaling. Compute depends on power and buildings, and an office floor supplies neither.

What the data does not cover is whether West Monroe runs any infrastructure elsewhere, or what cloud and hosting providers it uses. It also does not establish that no other miscategorized records exist in the Illinois set. It establishes only that this address should not be read as data center capacity.
